> A custom ESP32-based MP3 player featuring microSD storage, a PCM5102A DAC, an OLED display, physical buttons, and a rotary encoder. It will play locally stored music through a 3.5 mm audio jack, with a headphone amplifier added if needed. Designed for offline playback, modularity, and future upgrades.

#  MP3 Player Devlog
## This Journal contains work from the last 2 days.

Started working on the schematic for my ESP32 MP3 player today. Somehow this went from “wouldn't it be funny if I built my own music player” to spending my time fighting KiCad. Anyway, here's the progress.

**1. The components**

ESP32, PCM5102 DAC, SD card reader, OLED, buttons, rotary encoder. The usual suspects.

![Untitled design](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/9db6ad2ef0c99b682a52f5ddbf4dbe859b964be8488d52d4d73ec80f840b5605.jpg)

AND YES THIS WAS MADE IN CANVA, WAGE A WAR ON ME IF YOU WANT!

**2. Making symbols**

Some components didn't have the symbols I needed, so I made my own. Because apparently drawing little boxes and naming pins is my life now.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/a9fe152bbbdbe8e628349924021104bf0effca9852cacb757e8b366385c09ba3.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/7cc90ed393c3945c829a3a78fe32e394ff5b2697c16d584070ea7dfc2379ef22.png)

**3. Footprint shenanigans**

Downloaded the DAC footprint and modified it, including fixing the pin numbering to match my symbol. One wrong pin and the PCB becomes an expensive piece of modern art. The SD card on the other hand was easy to make, just a 6pin connector with 2.54mm pitch and some silkscreen borders.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/13abed9e2c0fbd971846b703388f41bc142fdcddc727143e316196249390115f.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/e9b3ec2997ae66d08b95fc023cdf2b9ba905c1b6c03866ae139dca3001958dd5.png)

**4. The controls**

Added the buttons and rotary encoder for playback and navigation. Slowly starting to look like an actual device.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/e8c27e6d3e3e3053ebd4ffcd2d143e79eb273dc26586e8a9f11fa02ebdccf36d.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/164c3e7c5916e5c83c5573e6c71cd0bd660e3ae667d4e774c7678023df2d361b.png)

Connected everything and finished the schematic. PCB design is next. Then comes the fun part: discovering everything I did wrong.

### 2026-10-30: # MP3 Player Devlog 2

**4h**

# MP3 Player Devlog 2
## PCB layout and routing, about 4 hours of work.

The schematic was the easy part. Turns out drawing wires between boxes is a lot less stressful than figuring out where the boxes physically go. This session was all about turning the schematic into an actual board.

**1. Choosing the layout**

My main question was whether this should be a one-sided board with everything crammed on top or a two-sided sandwich. I went with the sandwich:

- **Top side:** the stuff you touch and look at, which is the OLED, the buttons and the rotary encoder.
- **Bottom side:** the stuff you don't need to see, which is the ESP32, the SD card module and the PCM5102 DAC.

This keeps the board small enough to hold like an actual music player instead of a circuit board with a screen on it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/49b2ca35e1704846d7596a9308f438232c4251de0a7865db699d4371cdfe6980.png)

**2. Placing the big parts first**

The ESP32 went down first since everything else connects to it. I put it so the antenna end sits at the edge of the board, because copper and ground pour near the antenna ruin the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth range. The SD card module went on the right with its slot facing the board edge so the card can actually be removed. The DAC went near the top, away from the SD card's noisy SPI lines.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/ff998421f97b5b938a3f5f81a40c92363d01ce91604f891f51d7c0eb50aafb8e.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/71dc65bf15833d09897422ada731b23582ab498aea3be85046c02c63fbff31fc.png)

**3. The controls**

Four buttons in a T shape (previous, play/pause, next, and a menu button under the middle one), with the rotary encoder at the bottom right where a thumb would naturally land. The OLED sits above all of that. I'm not claiming it's perfectly ergonomic, but it should feel like a real device.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/e8ab44ad28b0f5b195090386e34911c98cef6e34ffc414b612ff6d15c999ada8.png)

**4. SD card shenanigans**

My first SD module placement had its angled header tails running straight into the ESP32. I decided I wasn't going to use the angled header anyway, and the module in the layout is basically a placeholder for the real connection, so I'm treating it as a mockup for now.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/f3ba1663de8c87f16c916cf024b04420f1dcdaebda05719d2fd3160d09fcad75.png)

**5. Routing**

This is where the 4 hours really went. The main things I was trying to do:

- Keep the I2S lines (BCK, LRCK, DIN) short and away from the SD card's SPI lines, since mixing a fast clock with audio is a good way to hear it later.
- Keep the OLED I2C and button lines tidy, because they don't care much as long as they connect.
- Pour ground on both layers and stitch it together with vias, so signals have a clean return path and there are no isolated copper islands.
- Keep copper out from under the ESP32 antenna.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/075ce1f65b39c6246b82593a00359de10d61f0b4bbca24f94527c6fce51ae665.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/9b6afc5b62b23b228319928c019de7cdadf823afd37022b9e9b15efda11f10f6.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/9b6afc5b62b23b228319928c019de7cdadf823afd37022b9e9b15efda11f10f6.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/45765ad92a8bc9160bbcf5d88c8f750d0996f6ea1e9b931d644e00d61cb1eb8f.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/74460a73ce72e35e9511cfd5e8465487fb453858ac51f32f71dbc0b6d8a12af3.png)

**6. Next**

CAD and Firmware, for CAD I can figure something out but for the firmware I have to read some more docs.

### 2026-11-01: # Changed the PCB a bit, and found listings and links for all parts.

**2.25h**

# Changed the PCB a bit, and found listings and links for all parts.

So, this is something I needed to do after realizing the button footprint I chose before is not something that is very abundant in most electronic retailer's armory. Even in the rare few listings available in my country cost a LOT i am talking like 0.5USD with a MOQ of 20. So I switched to a standard 6x6x8 mm button footprint which is much more available.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/34197692ca07037f0a15f3ce57ea80cbc8e1497ef61c83d62bde4ff5003be417.png)

Also I realized that I would be needing some mounting holes for the case. Which led me to use m2 mounting holes on the two corners of the board at a distance of 4mm of either end.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/bd621ecd8612b98bafff1f3ccbbb6c9f0908cc7468698dbbe4e73a7ea6acf598.png)

Finally about the listings, it was genuinely VERY HARD to find the listings for a esp32 which had the footprint I used in the project, eventually with the help of Gemini and Claude i found a suitable ESP32 board.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/cafd2ccd4ebc83ce3fe456f3d5f28d2d8b4991c872dbc58c4437cbf3b313349f.png)

Anyway this is how the BOM looks now!
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/26b02f87da6eba121ee456c3315bd11fae5ce2fdbcd799f9eb1ffb3226bce713.png)

# ITS CADIN TIME!

# MP3 Player Devlog 3
## This journal contains about 2.25 hours of work.

The PCB is routed, which means my music player is now a very fancy circuit board with no way to hold it. Time to give it a body. This session was all about designing the case in Onshape.

**1. The plan**

The case is two parts: a main body that holds the board, and a separate front plate that the screen and controls poke through. The whole thing is going to be 3D printed, because of course it is.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/88c0cbb1353b02d930d4dbc8371eb206d200777974b616f5bc9bf0488add1f26.png)

**2. The case body**

Here's the top view of the body. It's a rounded rectangle with an inner wall offset, leaving a hollow for the PCB. There are two notches along the top edge, which are the holes for the aux jack and the USB-B port. I also added two circular features at the bottom corners [what are these, e.g. standoffs or screw bosses?].

The PCB mounts inside using heat set inserts and M2 screws, so I'm not just hoping the board stays put.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/0af56f5900e298740effa6c2ab73b2bf6170b7d3843c6af26e320d73eebf7b41.png)

**3. The front plate**

The plate has three cutouts:

- **OLED window:** a square opening for the display.
- **Button cutout:** a T-shaped opening that matches the T layout of the four buttons.
- **Encoder cutout:** a square opening at the bottom right for the rotary encoder.

I made it by drawing the cutouts on the Edge.Cuts layer in KiCad, directly over the real footprints, so the openings line up with the parts. Then I exported it as a DXF and brought it into Onshape.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/08e11d8e5a318c224834102613129412637f46996740f7d8eb7edaf0244e6303.png)

**4. Putting it together**

In the 3D view, the display, the button cluster and the encoder all show through their cutouts. The T-shaped button opening came out nicely, and it's clear which button is which.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/cac9b5013f074379b357fd7ecce90e90d35a5abf3258843e491e1e13b4ed4f6a.png)

**5. Next**

I have to make the repo and write the repo!
